title: Frontiers: Estimating the Long-Term Impact of Major Events on Consumption Patterns: Evidence from COVID-19
eligible_reason: Methods paper with an age-period-cohort style model around one common event (COVID-19, March 2020). felm(log(outcome) ~ 0 | cohort_week + cohort + week) on customer-acquisition-cohort x calendar-week cells, with cohort-by-post interactions for heterogeneity and seasonality regressions (splines, holiday dummies) on the estimated period effects. Cohorts are acquisition cohorts, not treatment-adoption cohorts; every cohort is exposed to the event at the same calendar date. No staggered binary treatment.
design_notes: R. replication_code/replication code.R on inputs/agg_data_<category>.csv (nine non-subscription categories, cohort-week level).
data_provenance_note: README: Earnest Analytics data anonymized with differential-privacy Laplace noise on logged spend, re-standardized, aggregated to cohort-week, indexed by total acquisitions, and rounded.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Single event, not a DiD with staggered adoption.
